claims.wording: Shiny is THEODORE HQ's menu-bar memory utility for Mac.
claims.excerpt: Shiny, the one-tap memory cleanup app for Mac, lives quietly in your menu bar.

claims.wording: The vendor specifies macOS 13 Ventura or newer, Apple Silicon and Intel, using one Universal binary.
claims.excerpt: Shiny needs macOS 13 (Ventura) or newer, on Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4) or Intel. ... Shiny is a Universal binary
claims.conditions: No installation or hardware compatibility test performed. No Windows/Linux support inferred.

claims.wording: Shiny says it does not index your disk and cannot fix slowness caused by a full disk or ageing hardware.
claims.excerpt: it doesn't index your disk. ... If it's slow from a full disk or aging hardware, Shiny can't fix that.
claims.conditions: Supports adjacent classification, not proof that every undocumented storage feature is absent.

claims.wording: Polish is documented to free inactive memory, refresh stale DNS lookups and optionally close hidden apps without open windows.
claims.excerpt: Shiny frees the inactive memory apps no longer need, refreshes stale DNS lookups, and, if you've asked it to, closes hidden apps with no open windows.
claims.conditions: No measured speed, memory recovery or safety claim.

claims.wording: Auto-polish is documented as off by default, pressure-triggered when enabled, at most once per five minutes, skipping the memory clear during audio playback.
claims.excerpt: It's off by default. With it on, Shiny polishes by itself while your Mac is under memory pressure, at most once every five minutes, and it skips the memory clear while audio is playing.
claims.conditions: Not storage-growth monitoring or saved per-path cleanup approval.

claims.wording: Sneaky Apps may move a startup entry chosen by the user; the vendor documents Undo.
claims.excerpt: The one thing it moves is a startup entry you choose to set aside in Sneaky Apps, and Undo puts it back.
claims.conditions: Do not repeat unconditional never touches files marketing; do not test by disabling startup items.

claims.wording: The advertised price is $4.99 once; official offer metadata specifies USD, and the personal licence covers up to three personally used Macs.
claims.excerpt: One-time. $4.99 once, on up to three Macs, forever.
claims.conditions: Tax depends on country and final checkout price; no checkout opened or purchase tested. Future-major-update entitlement is disputed separately in C08.

claims.wording: All future updates are included forever.

claims.conditions: Do not assert all future major releases are free. Require official reconciliation or independent editorial approval of explicitly conflict-qualified wording; no contact sent.

claims.wording: The vendor documents update checks and Polar licence checks, including up to seven days offline between checks.

workflow.title: Before pressing Polish: separate Mac memory pressure from a full disk
workflow.primaryIntent: Diagnose whether a sluggish Mac calls for RAM/background-app attention or storage investigation before choosing a utility.
workflow.leadDirection: Choose the diagnostic path before a cleanup button. Shiny targets memory/background activity; do not treat its output as disk space recovered.
sections: Use Activity Monitor Memory Pressure, Cached Files and Swap Used rather than treating all occupied RAM as waste (C12).
Map documented Polish, optional Auto-polish and Sneaky Apps actions to that diagnosis (C04–C06); do not execute changes during research.
When a full disk is the problem, switch to storage investigation rather than expecting Shiny to fix it (C03).
Compare read-only app/helper investigation in Breathing Room, which we build, with Shiny's narrower action workflow (C13–C14).
List licence conflict, online checks, preview caveats and built-in Activity Monitor as the no-purchase diagnostic path.
workflow.interactionPass: A non-destructive decision checklist: memory pressure concern / full-disk concern / uncertain; link to Apple's guide and explain what each signal means. No auto-close or filesystem deletion controls; no arbitrary code tutorial.
workflow.visualPlan: After lead: approved real Shiny app view, pending; later: selected labeled Breathing Room Apps example preview. Link the official demo while blocked, not as a replacement for the required image.

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs Shiny: storage investigation or memory Polish?
comparison.primaryIntent: Choose between adjacent Mac workflows, not a universal cleaner winner.
rows: Price, three-Mac licence and unresolved major-update promise (C07–C08)
Breathing Room free preview, hosted paid AI and grouped monitoring boundaries (C13–C14)
comparison.shinyAdvantages: Documented compact menu-bar workflow, optional pressure-triggered action, three personal Macs for an advertised one-time fee; vendor publishes notarization claim. None are independently tested outcomes.
comparison.shinyTradeoffs: Not a full-disk remedy per vendor; licence-check/offline conditions; major-update entitlement conflict; no verified evidence for storage-growth investigation or developer-cache tooling.
comparison.breathingRoomAdvantages: Source-backed storage exploration and grouped app/helper inspection address a different diagnostic task, with free local core documented in the current register.
comparison.breathingRoomTradeoffs: Preview, not Developer ID signed/notarized in current release disclosure; Python 3.10+ disk inventory requirement; limited binary/hardware validation; hosted AI requires account/internet, shares relevant diagnostic context and has an optional recurring paid offer. No measured superiority or RAM-purge parity established.
